baseline_findings.summary: Imperial cylinder constraints use max 1766 ft3 and retain metric min/step, rejecting defaults while permitting impossible gas volumes.
Travel manual depth limits disagree between markup, metric restore, and imperial mode.
Rounded display values become canonical physical inputs; Best Mix and CNS now reproduce the same unit-roundtrip drift.
Min-deco regression checks an adapter property rather than observable schedule behavior.
Cycle history allowed unresolved findings and a blocked prior record to be deleted or rewritten as passed.
Knowledge Base states that extending shallow stops is safe without qualifying oxygen exposure, gas reserve, or plan-recalculation limits.
Cycle 3 regressions compare rounded outputs and restore values before units, masking physical-depth drift and corrupting test state.
VPM-B+GFS copy says it helps when shallow stops feel too long, contradicting the app's accurate description that GFS adds a conservative surface ceiling.

findings.root_cause: User input and stepper writers update displayed values without refreshing the data-depth-m or data-volume-l canonical state consumed after a unit switch.
findings.failure_path: Switch to imperial, edit a depth or cylinder size, then switch units again; consumers continue using the pre-edit physical value and the UI reverts the edit.
findings.impact: Best Mix, CNS, contingency, export, planner depth, and gas-volume calculations can use stale physical inputs.
findings.evidence: Independent Chromium traces reproduce stale 30 m/40 m/12 L canonical values after visible edits to 120 ft/134 ft/0.5 ft3.
findings.recommendation: Give every canonicalized control one writer contract and test input, stepper, restore, and both unit-roundtrip paths through the final consumer.

findings.root_cause: The manual ledger was allowed to claim SEVEN_LENS_REVIEWED without running the protocol close validator over every reviewed cycle.
findings.failure_path: Cycle records lack required evidence and fail close validation while the ledger and documentation still report PASSED.
findings.impact: A release can present incomplete or stale review evidence as a completed safety audit.
findings.evidence: check --phase close fails Cycles 2-4; Cycle 4 has no evidence_runs and its five closed findings have empty evidence_ids.
findings.recommendation: Run check-all from the static audit gate and require ledger-record-commit parity before a reviewed status is accepted.

findings.root_cause: Cycle 2/3 regression setup mutates canonical DOM datasets and persistent settings without restoring the complete pre-test state.
findings.failure_path: Run the complete engine suite; later contingency cases inherit altered travel-depth and canonical input state.
findings.impact: The suite is order-dependent and current CI fails CYCLE31-CONTINGENCY-MOD and CYCLE33-PPO2-TOXICITY.
findings.evidence: Current dev engine regression reports 166 passed and 2 failed; a browser suite probe leaves travelGasManualDepth at 322 ft.
findings.recommendation: Snapshot and restore values, datasets, units, storage, and globals around every case; add shuffled-order and repeated-run cleanliness gates.

findings.root_cause: Trace evidence previously allowed forced tested actions, empty/vacuous assertions, one execution, non-finite captures, and no console or page-error gate.
findings.failure_path: A trace can bypass visibility or event behavior and still be cited as proof of a user-visible fix.
findings.impact: Cursor can close findings with evidence that does not reproduce an actual interactive consumer path.
findings.evidence: The prior Cycle 3 trace passed a unit switch but never edited the control after switching, so it missed SL-C04-H-02.
findings.recommendation: Require schema-validated, repeated real interactions, finite captures, state restoration, console cleanliness, and artifact-backed assertions.
